metadata.notes: Date-focused core corroboration; historic/estimated numerical values, license checks, original station observations and event time zone all require final human review.

reviews.title_after: Paris floods as the Seine rises toward its historic 1910 crest
reviews.location_after: Paris and the Seine River basin, France
reviews.secondary_publisher: French National Archives of the World of Work
reviews.core_fact: Flooded Paris streets were photographed on January 27, 1910 as the Seine was approaching its record January 28 crest; the river's rise followed saturated antecedent conditions and multiple precipitation episodes.
reviews.source_dependence: The 27 January dated museum photograph provides direct archival date/location evidence; National Archives Railway documentation independently gives the 28 January hydrometric maximum. The photographic rights statement is item-specific, not blanket clearance.
reviews.unverified_cautions: January 27 is NOT the 8.62-m Austerlitz crest, which was January 28. Historic gauge datum and contemporaneous rounding differ (8.60 vs 8.62 meters). Do not treat dated photographic subject as direct proof of gauge height, and keep artifact license checks separate.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Jan 26–29 Seine stage trace with dated Jan27 museum-photo location marker and clearly labeled Jan28 crest

reviews.title_after: An EF4 tornado tears across Iowa near Winterset during the March 2022 outbreak
reviews.core_fact: A long-track EF4 tornado touched down near Macksburg, Iowa on March 5, 2022 and moved toward Winterset and central Iowa.
reviews.source_dependence: Original NCEI Macksburg segment and NWS Des Moines post-storm survey rely on the same tornado damage survey; separate NWS web location is not independent EF rating measurement.
reviews.unverified_cautions: This NCEI entry is the Macksburg segment, not a second distinct EF4. EF rating is based on damage indicators, not a direct sustained wind reading. The tornado outbreak includes multiple distinct tracks.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Macksburg-to-Winterset tornado segment map with county boundaries and survey-rated damage locations

reviews.title_after: Farm-field dust blinds drivers along Illinois's Interstate 55
reviews.location_after: I-55 between Sangamon and Montgomery Counties, central Illinois
reviews.core_fact: On May 1, 2023, strong winds lofted recently tilled field dust into the I-55 corridor south of Springfield, Illinois, reducing visibility and contributing to a severe multi-vehicle crash.
reviews.source_dependence: NOAA Storm Data and NWS Lincoln meteorological analysis share storm reports; news and Illinois State Police crash tallies would supply independent vehicle counts later.
reviews.unverified_cautions: NWS seasonal review cites 72 vehicles but police counts/incident revisions should be verified before publishing. Do not confuse this 2023 Illinois I-55 dust event with the Oct 23, 2023 Louisiana I-55 smoke-fog crash.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original farm-field footprint, wind-direction and highway map with agency timestamps and dust source/visibility mechanism

reviews.title_after: Torrential rain and landslides inundate Pago Pago, American Samoa
reviews.location_after: Pago Pago, Nuuuli and Tutuila Island, American Samoa
reviews.core_fact: Floods and rain-triggered landslides affected several Tutuila Island communities, including Pago Pago, on May 19, 2003.
reviews.source_dependence: Contemporaneous Associated Press coverage separately confirms dated flooding and local police reports; the news and NCEI casualty accounts may rely on shared first-responder information.
reviews.unverified_cautions: NCEI local excerpt specifically reports a landslide killing 3 men; contemporaneous news reports 4 deaths across American Samoa. The distinction is geographic/incident scope and should not be treated as contradictory until all deaths classified. No precise hourly rain gauge verified.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Tutuila mountain drainage map showing rainfall-driven Pago Pago flooding and separate landslide impact sites

reviews.title_before: Excessive Heat — TOHONO O ODHAM NATION, Arizona
reviews.title_after: A deadly tornado hits New Richmond, Wisconsin as a circus crowds the town
reviews.location_after: New Richmond, St. Croix County, Wisconsin
reviews.secondary_publisher: Wisconsin Historical Society dated photographic archive
reviews.core_fact: The June 12, 1899 New Richmond tornado struck on the first afternoon of a circus visit to the community, leaving extensive devastation; the Wisconsin Historical Society retains dated original photographs.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Wisconsin historical synthesis and Wisconsin Historical Society primary image metadata are distinct material types, but historical fatality totals are drawn from overlapping nineteenth-century accounts.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The 117 deaths commonly cited is historically reconstructed, not a modern standardized disaster census. The historic storm was called a cyclone, but it was a tornado. Historic photographs list Wisconsin Historical Society as rights holder; do not assume copyright or reuse permission.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original hand-plotted 1899 New Richmond town street plan and historic tornado path with annotated circus gathering area

reviews.title_after: An exceptionally violent F5 tornado strikes Oakfield, Wisconsin
reviews.location_after: Oakfield and adjacent Fond du Lac County, Wisconsin
reviews.core_fact: On July 18, 1996, a violent F5 tornado struck the Oakfield area of Wisconsin; satellite analysis places the tornado around 0015 UTC July 19, corresponding to the evening of July 18 locally.
reviews.source_dependence: NCEI Oakfield section and NWS local damage path are the same original survey lineage; GOES-8 imagery independently confirms cloud/storm context but not ground-level F5 wind speed.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Use historic F5 (old Fujita scale), NOT EF5. Local date July 18 versus 0015 UTC July 19 is a time-zone conversion, not two event dates. Top F5 rating is limited to surveyed damage segment east of Oakfield.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original F5 damage-track transect over 1996 GOES-8 storm-scale satellite cloud context with local/UTC clocks

reviews.title_after: A rapidly spreading fire traps smokejumpers in Montana's Mann Gulch
reviews.location_after: Mann Gulch, Helena National Forest, Montana
reviews.core_fact: The Mann Gulch wildfire was discovered and fought on August 5, 1949 near Helena, Montana, and extreme fire behavior trapped a smokejumper crew; the incident killed thirteen firefighters.
reviews.source_dependence: USFS Fire Lab account and Forest History Society contextual history derive from overlapping incident investigations; NWCG staff ride supplies a dedicated separate weather-behavior teaching context.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Lightning ignition may have occurred August 4; August 5 is fire discovery and entrapment anniversary. Do not attribute exact wind or RH from a distant ranger station to the fire front. Firefighter fatalities are 13; a subsequently reported investigator's death months later is not part of this immediate count.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Mann Gulch topographic slope cross-section and fire spread timeline with surface heating/upslope wind concepts from documented fire research

reviews.title_after: Hurricane Carol strikes southern New England with damaging coastal surge
reviews.location_after: Long Island, coastal Connecticut, Rhode Island and Massachusetts
reviews.secondary_publisher: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management
reviews.core_fact: Hurricane Carol struck Long Island and southern New England, including southeastern Connecticut, on August 31, 1954, causing severe coastal wind and surge impacts around Narragansett Bay.
reviews.source_dependence: NHC storm history and Rhode Island state coastal flood climatology represent different institutional syntheses but common historic observations and tide marks.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Carol and Edna struck New England in the same 1954 season but were separate storms. A 3-category rating at coastal landfall is historical best track; downtown Providence 8–10 foot water depths are not a uniform regional storm surge height. Local tide, datum, exact landfall center and impact numbers need checking.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Aug31 1954 Carol track and Narragansett Bay surge-funneling schematic with separate historic tide-datum markings

reviews.title_after: Separate flash floods overrun Hildale and Zion's Keyhole Canyon
reviews.location_after: Hildale/Short Creek and Keyhole Canyon, Zion National Park, southwest Utah
reviews.core_fact: On September 14, 2015, violent flash flooding struck the Hildale/Short Creek drainages recorded in the NCEI Grafton zone entry and separately overtook a group in Zion National Park's Keyhole Canyon.
reviews.source_dependence: NCEI Utah zone flood narrative and Zion NPS victim chronology are different agency impact sites during the same regional rain event; they do not independently verify water level at the same location.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Hildale and Zion's Keyhole Canyon are geographically distinct drainages. Do not assign the seven Keyhole fatalities to Hildale or vice versa. Utah Geological Survey's general page has an apparent 2014/2015 year typo: use National Park Service exact Sept14 2015 date. Never infer an individual warning receipt or evacuation decision from issued warning timestamp alone.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Hildale versus Keyhole drainage-separation map with NWS 20:22Z flood-warning overlay and park-specific 2015 incident times

reviews.title_after: A wind-driven wildfire destroys Peshtigo on the night Chicago also burns
reviews.location_after: Peshtigo, Marinette County and Door Peninsula, Wisconsin
reviews.core_fact: On the evening of October 8, 1871, the Peshtigo Fire spread rapidly through drought-parched northeastern Wisconsin amid strong winds, devastating Peshtigo on October 8–9 during the same regional fire outbreak as the Great Chicago Fire.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Green Bay historical overview and Wisconsin State Climatology Office provide separate atmospheric synthesis based on sparse nineteenth-century weather records and eyewitness reports.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Historical fire death totals are uncertain, with credible estimates ~1,200 to ~1,500 across affected communities. Do not claim fire tornadoes and fire-driven oxygen depletion were instrument-measured. Distinguish regional Peshtigo/other concurrent fires from Chicago fire ignition legend.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original October 8 regional pressure-gradient and wind direction reconstruction marking Peshtigo and Chicago as distinct fires, with uncertain historic contours clearly labeled

reviews.title_after: Category 4 Hurricane Hazel makes landfall near the Carolina state line
reviews.location_after: Calabash, North Carolina and Horry/Brunswick Counties on the Carolina coast
reviews.core_fact: Hurricane Hazel made landfall near the North Carolina–South Carolina border on October 15, 1954 as a Category 4 hurricane and quickly moved inland.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Wilmington and NHC historical storm accounts use common Weather Bureau and modern hurricane reanalysis; two URLs do not imply independent best-track intensity measurement.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not cite a modern EF rating for Hazel hurricane winds. Exact 18-foot water level may refer to local surge/tide combination and site, not entire coastline. Haiti and Canadian fatality figures are separate from U.S. landfall statistics. The historic coastline crossing was near Calabash/SC border, not all of Wilmington.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Oct15 landfall and storm tide reconstruction from Weather Bureau maps with tide datum and state border annotated

reviews.title_after: A predawn F3 tornado strikes communities south of Evansville
reviews.location_after: Vanderburgh, Warrick and Spencer Counties, southwest Indiana and northwest Kentucky
reviews.core_fact: A long-track F3 tornado crossed northwest Kentucky and southern Indiana near Evansville before dawn on November 6, 2005.
reviews.source_dependence: NCEI Evansville local segment and NWS Paducah full-track survey share the same NOAA tornado reports; adding a second page does not independently measure 41-mile tornado path.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Use F3, not EF3 (pre-2007 scale). The specific NCEI Evansville segment is not a different tornado from the larger multistate path. Fatality and injury counts depend on direct versus indirect and affected-county definitions.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original time-resolved tornado route past Ellis Park and southern Evansville with area warning issue time and local clock labels

reviews.title_after: The Portland Gale batters New England as the steamship Portland is lost
reviews.location_after: Boston-to-Portland sea route and coastal New England, United States
reviews.core_fact: A destructive coastal winter storm struck New England November 26–27, 1898, and the steamship Portland was lost at sea on November 27.
reviews.source_dependence: NOAA Stellwagen shipwreck record independently documents the marine loss date; the NWS historical weather-map synthesis supports the concurrent gale. Archival sailing-time accounts disagree and are not verified by marine sensor.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The gale spans November 26–27. Departure timing conflicts between the National Archives article (Nov27) and other maritime histories (Nov26), so do not state the exact sailing day or hour. Historic death/shipwreck totals are uncertain and reported differently; use only the ship loss core event.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original November 26–27 1898 storm-center/ship-route map with harbor and shipwreck positions marked as approximate

reviews.title_after: The Hanukkah Eve windstorm intensifies across western Washington
reviews.location_after: Puget Sound, Seattle and Bremerton, Washington
reviews.core_fact: A powerful extratropical cyclone brought damaging winds to western Washington on December 14–15, 2006, popularly known as the Hanukkah Eve Windstorm.
reviews.source_dependence: HistoryLink contemporaneous/historical community accounts and NOAA Storm Data draw from different documentary paths; peer-reviewed synoptic research reconstructs the cyclone but still uses some original weather observing network.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Event developed December 14 but many Puget Sound peak wind impacts and later carbon monoxide fatalities occurred December 15 or afterward. Avoid assigning the storm-wide mortality to December 14. Named Hanukkah Eve Storm has multiple locally timed phases.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original 14–15 Dec surface cyclone path and western Washington measured gust map showing midnight date boundary and exposure effects

reviews.title_before: Winter Storm — LOWER SNAKE RIVER PLAIN, Idaho
reviews.title_after: Cyclone Tracy turns toward Darwin as Christmas Eve warnings intensify
reviews.location_after: Darwin, Tiwi Islands and northern Australia
reviews.core_fact: On December 24, 1974, Cyclone Tracy turned toward Darwin and Darwin received a specific cyclone warning around 12:30 p.m. local time; its destructive eye and worst winds crossed Darwin overnight into Christmas Day December 25.
reviews.source_dependence: Australian Bureau of Meteorology track/warnings and Northern Territory public archives provide distinct agency histories but both derive cyclone operational records and historic testimony.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Tracy's most catastrophic landfall is EARLY DECEMBER 25, not December 24; December 24 is change of track, warning and pre-landfall arrival. The 217-km/h measured gust was recorded during the night before anemometer failure and should not be assigned to 12:30 pm warning time. Original NT historic photos/audio require item-level reuse review.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Dec 24 hourly forecast/track-warning timeline ending in Dec25 Darwin impact, with measured versus estimated gusts distinct

claim_checks.claim: Seine maximum water level of ~8.62 m at Pont d'Austerlitz occurred January 28, 1910
claim_checks.evidence: French National Archives railroad flood chronology dates peak January 28 and gives about 8.60 m
claim_checks.independence: Original public archive historical hydrometric chronology; datum and rounded values differ
claim_checks.caution: Never assign 8.62-m maximum to January 27; verify exact source and gauge datum
claim_checks.use: Do not use January 28 peak as January 27 observed crest

claim_checks.evidence: NWS Milwaukee historical review and Wisconsin Historical Society image metadata date the storm
claim_checks.independence: Historical NWS synthesis and archival primary photo catalog have distinct provenance

claim_checks.evidence: NWS Milwaukee and Wisconsin tornado historic rankings report 117
claim_checks.independence: Two NWS sources share historic fatality accounts rather than independent census
claim_checks.caution: Historic counting methods and record completeness unknown; attribute to NWS rather than absolute census

claim_checks.claim: Mann Gulch smokejumper disaster on August 5, 1949 killed thirteen firefighters
claim_checks.evidence: US Forest Service Fire Sciences history records 13 fatalities and the August 5 incident
claim_checks.independence: Agency history anchored in original investigation; Forest History Society another synthesis
claim_checks.caution: Lightning ignition occurred previous afternoon according to modern USFS account; do not label August 5 as ignition for certainty
claim_checks.use: Core disaster date and USFS-associated fatality count, not final human approved

claim_checks.claim: Mann Gulch wildfire ignition occurred August 5, 1949
claim_checks.evidence: USFS 75th anniversary article says ignition by lightning previous afternoon, Aug4, with detection Aug5
claim_checks.independence: USFS archival field history is original institutional reference
claim_checks.caution: Some retrospectives say 'fire broke out Aug5' while ignition was probably previous day
claim_checks.use: Do not use precise August 5 ignition assertion

claim_checks.claim: Hurricane Carol made landfall near Long Island and Connecticut on August 31, 1954
claim_checks.evidence: NHC historical summary and Rhode Island climatological storm history both date Carol's New England impacts Aug31
claim_checks.independence: NHC best-track/historic reanalysis, state impact record uses shared post-storm sources
claim_checks.caution: Careful not to substitute Hurricane Edna later in Sept1954; surge height depends on local tide datum
claim_checks.use: Core dated landfall and region statement

claim_checks.claim: Zion Keyhole Canyon and Hildale Utah floods were distinct impact locations on September 14, 2015
claim_checks.evidence: NPS names Keyhole Canyon Sept14 and NCEI Grafton/Hildale record details separate Short Creek flooding
claim_checks.independence: Independent park incident vs NCEI locality flood segment, but shared rain-producing system
claim_checks.caution: Do not treat Keyhole Canyon as Short Creek and do not combine fatalities as from one river
claim_checks.use: May mention separate locations; no localized stage figure verified

claim_checks.claim: Peshtigo Fire devastated northeastern Wisconsin on October 8–9, 1871
claim_checks.evidence: NWS Green Bay and University of Wisconsin state climatologists independently recount drought/wind weather setup
claim_checks.independence: Shared nineteenth-century reports, separate atmospheric synthesis
claim_checks.caution: Historic pressure map is reconstructed, not direct dense station network; distinguish separate Chicago fire

claim_checks.claim: Exactly 1,500 died in the Peshtigo Fire
claim_checks.evidence: NWS Green Bay broadly describes 1200+; Wisconsin Historical Society estimates about 1500 in regional total
claim_checks.independence: Historical reporting uncertainty makes precise casualty census unreliable
claim_checks.caution: Do not publish an unqualified exact total; clarify city vs region and historical count source

claim_checks.claim: Hurricane Hazel struck near North Carolina-South Carolina line at Category 4 on October 15, 1954
claim_checks.evidence: NWS Wilmington and NHC event records agree on date, category and border landfall
claim_checks.independence: Shared modern best-track and Weather Bureau source lineage
claim_checks.caution: Wind intensity is assessed 1-min tropical cyclone convention, not measured storm surge rating
claim_checks.use: Core storm date and historical category with source attribution

claim_checks.independence: Historical community source vs peer reviewed atmospheric reconstruction share some original observations
claim_checks.caution: Peak impacts, power outages and indirect carbon-monoxide deaths largely occurred Dec15 or later

claim_checks.independence: AP contemporary local police attribution vs storm-data zone account overlap some first responders
claim_checks.caution: Three site-specific victims versus four across region; check original coroner/police report for scope
